solutions.name: Plan mode

solutions.name: Task system / background tasks and worker chats

analysis: **The shape.** Replit Agent reads A4 · R2 · C2 · O0. Its power is documented in plain terms: Agent builds, runs, tests and publishes on its own, and with connectors it reads and writes to outside services such as BigQuery, Linear and Slack. Its controls are settings a person can see: background work waits for review by default, there is a button to halt it, and Enterprise admins choose the scopes builders can request.

**Why Openness reads "not yet evidenced".** Not for lack of documents. The rule for Documented is met three times over: the limits and failure cases are written down, the data Agent uses is described, and the model providers are listed. The Openness ladder is cumulative, and its first rung asks for one public statement that the agent tells the people it talks to that it is an AI. That one sentence would lift Openness to level 2 at once and move the stage from Building (8) to Scaling (10).

**Where the evidence is strongest.** The autonomy story is backed by named customers: Forbes, in an article on Replit's newsroom, reports that Zillow's employees made more than 7,000 apps with Replit over a year on about 600 seats, and Plaid built an SLA dashboard with Replit Agent that is now in use. Replit also publishes an llms.txt for its documentation and a skills directory where partners publish skills for Agent, so other agents and other companies can build on it.

**What we saw and did not count.** Replit states a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation; without a public report or scope that covers Agent, it is shown and not counted. Two of Autonomy level 4's facts are available rather than default (connectors and automatic apply), and the card marks them so.

**For readers.** The customer pages tell a consistent story of people outside engineering building internal tools: Rokt's 700 staff building 135 apps in a day, Leatherman's 119 apps from 147 employees. Those are Replit's figures, on Replit's pages, and are reported here as such.

article.title: Replit Agent on the GAMMA-Ray Spectrum: A4 · R2 · C2 · O0
article.standfirst: The first company report from the GAMMA-Ray studio reads Replit's agent from its public pages: it builds and publishes on its own, its controls are settings people can see, and one sentence stands between it and the next stage.
body: Replit, an event partner at Web Summit Lisbon 2026, is the first company in the GAMMA-Ray report series. Its agent turns a description in plain language into a running app inside a Replit project. We read it only from public sources, captured and hashed every page on 10 November 2026, and let the published rules compute the card.

**Autonomy 4, Orchestrates.** Agent handles the work from planning to deployment. With connectors it reads and writes to outside services, and background tasks can be set to apply their own changes. Named customers use it: Zillow's employees made more than 7,000 apps with Replit over a year, as Forbes reports; Plaid built an internal SLA dashboard with it.
**Reach 2, Integrated.** Connectors and MCP servers link Agent to tools such as BigQuery, Linear and Slack. A published agent interface with documented authorisation would be the next rung.

**Control 2, Configurable.** Background work waits for a person's review by default; a stop button halts Agent; Enterprise admins set the scopes builders can request. A public page on monitoring Agent in operation would reach level 3.

**Openness: not yet evidenced, and close.** Replit documents Agent's limits, the data it uses and its model providers, which meets the rule for level 2. The first rung asks for a public statement that the agent tells people it is an AI. One sentence would move the whole card from Building to Scaling.
The card is beta and Replit has not seen it. Replit can claim it and add evidence; corrections are dated and carried to the card, the report and this article.

pt.title: O Replit Agent no GAMMA-Ray Spectrum: A4 · R2 · C2 · O0
pt.standfirst: O primeiro relatório do estúdio GAMMA-Ray lê o agente do Replit a partir das suas páginas públicas: constrói e publica sozinho, os controlos são definições visíveis, e uma frase separa-o da fase seguinte.
body: O Replit, parceiro do Web Summit Lisboa 2026, é a primeira empresa da série de relatórios GAMMA-Ray. O seu agente transforma uma descrição em linguagem simples numa aplicação a funcionar. Lemos apenas fontes públicas, capturadas e com hash a 10 de novembro de 2026, e as regras publicadas calcularam o cartão.

**Autonomia 4.** O Agent age, não apenas responde; com conectores lê e escreve em serviços externos. Clientes identificados usam-no: os funcionários da Zillow fizeram mais de 7.000 aplicações em um ano, segundo a Forbes. **Alcance 2.** Conectores e servidores MCP ligam-no a ferramentas como BigQuery, Linear e Slack. **Controlo 2.** O trabalho em segundo plano aguarda revisão por defeito, há um botão para o parar e os administradores Enterprise definem os âmbitos de acesso.

**Abertura: ainda sem evidência, e perto.** O Replit documenta os limites do Agent, os dados que usa e os fornecedores de modelos. O primeiro degrau pede uma declaração pública de que o agente diz às pessoas que é uma IA. Uma frase levaria o cartão de Building para Scaling.
O cartão é beta e o Replit ainda não o viu. Pode reclamá-lo e acrescentar evidência; as correções são datadas.
